Hi Tessa,

Great to meet you at the partner sync last week. AcmeCloud is ready to push Redwood's offers into our AWS/Azure/GCP reseller catalog, but we need a concise mapping of: which SKUs should go to each cloud by region, the canonical pricing tiers we should display (entry / standard / enterprise), and any recommended canary regions for initial listings.

High-level asks from our side:
- A single spreadsheet with SKU -> cloud -> region -> recommended offer name.
- Canary criteria (what traffic % and telemetry signals you want us to watch).
- Any billing/contract nuances we should include in the marketplace listing (e.g., metered usage vs subscription).

Can your team share those by early next week? Happy to host a joint call to walk through.

Cheers,
Priya

Thanks Priya — we can definitely deliver that. Looping Ben (marketplace ops), Marissa (GTM/partner), and Lauren (regional ops) so we can put together the spreadsheet and canary runbook.

Initial notes from our side:
- We want to minimize SKU proliferation. Suggest 3 canonical offer SKUs per cloud: "Starter" (single-node, quantized), "Scale" (64-token throughput optimized), and "Enterprise" (reserved / dedicated throughput).
- Region split: prefer to list US-only Starter offers initially for all three clouds, expand EU/UK in phase 2. APAC to be gated on data residency requests and capacity.
- Canary regions: US-EAST-1 (AWS), East US (Azure), us-central1 (GCP) — choose mirrors so telemetry aligns.
- Pricing model: display list price per 1M tokens plus an optional monthly reserved capacity SKU for Enterprise. Metered default, subscription optional.

Ben/Marissa, can you take the lead on the SKU -> cloud -> region workbook and a one-page canary checklist? I added two deliverables: redwood-sku-routing-v1.xlsx and canary-onboarding-checklist.md.

Tessa Morgan
Head of Marketplace Partnerships | Redwood Inference

On Tue, Aug 31, 2027 at 09:05 AM Tessa Morgan <tessa_morgan@redwood.ai> wrote:
> Ben/Marissa, can you take the lead on the SKU -> cloud -> region workbook and a one-page canary checklist?

Started populating redwood-sku-routing-v1.xlsx — high level notes:
- SKU naming: use market-friendly labels, internal slug in parentheses (example: Starter (rdw-starter-v1)).
- Offer metadata: include required fields for AWS Marketplace (SaaS, metered billing flag, EULA link), Azure (Azure Marketplace Category), and GCP (Listing type).
- SKU to cloud mapping: we recommend publishing Starter on all three clouds in US regions. Scale only on AWS/GCP at launch (Azure listing to follow after validation). Enterprise (reserved) to be gated to AWS first because of our Dedicated infra parity.
- Canaries: pick low-traffic AZs within the major region (us-east-1a equivalent) and limit to 5% of traffic initially.

Open ops questions:
1) Can we keep identical SKU IDs across clouds to simplify analytics (Y/N)?
2) Does AcmeCloud require separate legal artifacts per cloud listing? Priya — can you clarify?

ben

Hi all — adding the GTM view and suggested canary telemetry thresholds.

Summary actions (GTM + Ops):
- Phase 0 (soft listing): Publish Starter on AWS/Azure/GCP in US regions only. Mark as "preview" and link to documentation.
- Phase 1 (canary): 0–5% traffic; watch latency P50/P95, token cost delta vs baseline, error rate >0.2% as a stop condition. Run canary for 72 hours minimum unless a stop condition is hit.
- Phase 2 (rollout): 5–50% over 2 weeks, expand EU/UK once SLA metrics stable.

Files attached: canary-onboarding-checklist.md (contains runbook), and a short CSV with offer names. Also pushed a Drive doc with the SKU mapping and the recommended marketing blurb to the shared folder: https://drive.google.com/redwood/marketplace-sku-routing

Notes for AcmeCloud: please confirm whether your listing UI requires separate price points per marketplace or if you will accept a single canonical price and display adjustments. If separate, we will provide per-cloud pricing columns in the workbook.

Thanks,
Marissa Cole
GTM Partnerships | Redwood Inference
